about.title: Personal Injury Help in Santa Clarita, California
about.longDescription: Santa Clarita covers a lot of ground, and most of it is reached by car. Soledad Canyon Road, Sierra Highway, Bouquet Canyon Road and McBean Parkway carry much of the daily traffic, and public collision records show those four corridors logging the highest counts of reported crashes in the city. For 2025, the most recent final year on record, Santa Clarita reported 706 injury collisions, 1,042 people hurt, and 14 traffic deaths. Reports tend to rise on Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. If one of those numbers now describes you, the paperwork that follows can feel heavier than the injury itself. Insurance adjusters call before the bruises fade. Medical bills arrive out of order. You may be unsure whether a claim is even worth pursuing. That is where LawProactive fits in. We are a free service, not a law firm. We do not give legal advice or handle cases. What we do is connect people in Santa Clarita and the rest of Los Angeles County with an independent personal injury attorney who can review what happened. The attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery. Reaching out costs nothing, and you decide what happens next.

whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your Santa Clarita Claim

items.title: The clock is usually two years
items.desc: Most California injury claims must be filed within two years of the incident. If a city, county, or state agency is involved, that window can shrink to six months, so timing matters more than people expect.

items.title: Partial fault does not shut you out
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault. If you were partly responsible, your recovery is reduced by your share, but you are not barred from bringing a claim.

items.title: No cap on pain-and-suffering in ordinary cases
items.desc: For a typical injury claim in California, there is no statutory limit on non-economic damages like pain, distress, and lost enjoyment of life. An attorney can explain how that applies to your situation.

items.title: Contingency means no upfront cost
items.desc: Attorneys in the LawProactive network are paid a percentage only if there is a recovery. If nothing is recovered, you owe no attorney fee.

items.question: Where do collisions in Santa Clarita tend to be reported?
items.answer: Public collision records show the highest counts along Soledad Canyon Road, Sierra Highway, Bouquet Canyon Road, and McBean Parkway. These are simply the corridors with the most reported crashes, which tracks with how much traffic they carry. Reports also tend to peak on Fridays between 3 p.m. and 5 p.m.

items.question: Is LawProactive a law firm?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people with an independent personal injury attorney. We do not give legal advice, represent clients, or take a portion of any recovery. Any attorney you speak with is independent of us.

items.question: How long do I have to file an injury claim in California?
items.answer: For most personal injury claims, California allows two years from the date of the injury. Claims against a government entity often have a much shorter deadline, sometimes just six months to file an administrative claim. Speaking with an attorney early helps make sure nothing lapses.

items.question: I think I was partly at fault. Can I still recover anything?
items.answer: Yes. California uses pure comparative fault, which means your recovery is reduced by your percentage of responsibility rather than eliminated. Even someone found mostly at fault can recover a portion of their damages.

items.question: What will it cost me to talk to an attorney?
